req.title: Logout clears session
req.statement: The system shall clear the session and redirect to / on GET /auth/logout.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /auth/logout must clear the session and redirect to /. I design tests covering: (1) positive path — authenticated user logs out, gets 302 to /, session cleared; (2) negative path — unauthenticated user hits logout, still gets 302 to / with no error (session.clear() on empty session is safe); (3) boundary/state-transition — user logs in, accesses a protected resource, logs out, then verifies the protected resource is no longer accessible (session truly cleared). Each test uses exact status codes and exact Location headers to catch operator/constant mutations. The STC test verifies the state machine: logged-in -> logged-out -> access denied.

tests.name: test_logout_authenticated_user_redirects_to_root_and_clears_session
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: Assert response status code is exactly 302
GET /create to verify session is cleared (should redirect to login)
expected: Subsequent access to login-required page redirects to /auth/login (session cleared)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login first
r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 on login, got {r_login.status_code}'
assert r_login.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Logout
r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert r_logout.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 on logout, got {r_logout.status_code}'
assert r_logout.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected Location=/, got {r_logout.headers.get("Location")}'

# Verify session is cleared: /create requires login, should redirect to /auth/login
r_create = client.get('/create')
assert r_create.status_code == 302
assert r_create.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

os.unlink(path)

actions: POST /auth/login with username=Anjali, password=cloud — transition to authenticated state

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# State 1: unauthenticated — /create must redirect to login
r_pre = client.get('/create')
assert r_pre.status_code == 302
assert r_pre.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

# Transition: login
r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302
assert r_login.headers['Location'] == '/'

# State 2: authenticated — /create must be accessible
r_auth = client.get('/create')
assert r_auth.status_code == 200

# Transition: logout
r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert r_logout.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r_logout.status_code}'
assert r_logout.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected /, got {r_logout.headers.get("Location")}'

# State 3: unauthenticated again — /create must redirect to login
r_post = client.get('/create')
assert r_post.status_code == 302
assert r_post.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

os.unlink(path)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')

# Exact status code — catches 301/303/200 mutations
assert r_logout.status_code == 302, f'Expected exactly 302, got {r_logout.status_code}'
assert r_logout.status_code != 301
assert r_logout.status_code != 303

# Exact Location — catches redirect-target mutations
location = r_logout.headers.get('Location', '')
assert location == '/', f'Expected exactly /, got {location!r}'
assert location != '/auth/login'
assert location != '/auth'
assert location != ''

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_logout_session_user_id_absent_after_logout
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User Diya (id=4, password=cloud) is logged in
actions: Inspect session to confirm user_id is set
Inspect session to confirm user_id is absent
expected: After logout: session does not contain user_id
trace: R-FLASKR-011: session cleared — verified by inspecting session cookie contents
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login and verify session has user_id
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess  # clean start

r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert r_login.status_code == 302

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' in sess, 'user_id should be in session after login'
    assert sess['user_id'] == 4, f'Expected user_id=4, got {sess.get("user_id")}'

# Logout
r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
assert r_logout.status_code == 302
assert r_logout.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Verify session is cleared
with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess, 'user_id must not be in session after logout'

os.unlink(path)
